findings.evidence: `<meta charset="utf-8">` is present but there is no `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">`
findings.fix: Add `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">` to the `<head>`.
findings.violation: Without a viewport meta tag, mobile browsers will render the form at desktop width and auto-zoom, and the later inline `font-size:16px` hack (meant to prevent iOS zoom-on-focus) has no effect without it.

findings.evidence: `<input id="street-input" name="street_address" type="text" autocomplete="address-line1" ... required="">` with no accompanying city, state/region, or country fields
findings.fix: Add city, state/region, and country fields (with `autocomplete="address-level2"`, `address-level1`, `country"`) grouped with street address and postal code.
findings.violation: The address is collected as a single street line plus a later, disconnected postal-code field, with no way to capture city, state, or country - incomplete for shipping an order.

findings.evidence: `<input id="phone2-input" name="phone_secondary" type="tel" autocomplete="tel">` - identical to the primary phone field's `autocomplete="tel"`
findings.fix: Differentiate the fields, e.g. wrap each in a `<fieldset>` with distinct autocomplete scoping, or drop autocomplete from the secondary field.
findings.violation: Both the primary and secondary phone inputs share the same `autocomplete="tel"` token, so browsers can't distinguish them and may autofill the same number into both.

findings.fix: Remove the field, or make it optional and only show it for business accounts.
findings.violation: A "Company website" field is a business/B2B field with no apparent relevance to a consumer apparel account signup, and it's marked required, blocking ordinary customers from completing signup.

findings.evidence: `<input id="member-input" ... inputmode="numeric" placeholder="Must be 8 digits" required="">`
findings.fix:
Add `maxlength="8"` and `pattern="\d{8}"`, and move the format instruction into persistent helper text (like the phone field's `

`) rather than relying solely on the placeholder.
findings.violation: The "must be 8 digits" instruction exists only as placeholder text, which disappears once the user starts typing, and there's no `pattern`/`maxlength` to actually enforce or validate the 8-digit requirement.

findings.evidence: `<label id="acctnum-label" for="acctnum-input">Account number</label>` immediately follows the "Membership number (8 digits)" field
findings.fix: Either merge these into one field or add label/help text clarifying the distinct purpose of each, and add appropriate validation/autocomplete attributes.
findings.violation: "Account number" and "Membership number" appear to refer to the same concept with no explanation of how they differ, and account number has no autocomplete attribute or format guidance at all.
Without a `name` attribute, the selected shipping speed will not be included in the submitted form data at all.

findings.fix: Remove one of the two redundant options (or rename to clearly distinct tiers, e.g. "Next-day" vs "Same-day").
findings.violation: "Overnight" and "Next-day" describe the same delivery speed, creating a confusing duplicate choice for users.

findings.evidence: `<label id="legalname-label" for="legalname-input">Your name</label> ... autocomplete="name" ... required=""`, compared to `row-name`'s `<label id="name-label" for="name-input">Full name</label>`
findings.fix: Remove this duplicate field, or rename/clarify its purpose if it's meant to capture something different (e.g. a legal name differing from a preferred name) and explain that distinction in the label.
findings.violation: This field duplicates the "Full name" field collected earlier in the form (same `autocomplete="name"`), forcing the user to enter their name twice with no explanation of why two name fields exist.

findings.fix: Move styling into a shared stylesheet/rule applied consistently to all inputs, and make "Organization name" optional (or remove it) for a consumer signup.
findings.violation: This input has an inline style not applied consistently to any other input in the form, and the field is required despite the form otherwise targeting individual consumers, not organizations.

findings.evidence: `<label id="contacttime-label" for="contacttime-input" style="display:block">Preferred contact time</label><input id="contacttime-input" name="contact_time" type="text" required="">`
findings.fix: Replace the free-text input with a `<select>` of time ranges (e.g. Morning/Afternoon/Evening) or a `<input type="time">`, and move the `display:block` styling to shared CSS.
findings.violation: "Preferred contact time" is captured as unconstrained free text, which will produce inconsistent, unparseable data, and the label has a one-off inline style not used elsewhere.

findings.evidence: `<button id="viewdetails-btn" type="button" style="padding:12px 20px;font-size:16px">View details</button>` placed directly before the submit button, with no script or handler anywhere in the document
findings.fix: Either implement its intended behavior with a script, or remove the button if it serves no function.
findings.violation: This button has no associated behavior (no `onclick`, no JS elsewhere in the document), so clicking it does nothing, and its prominent inline styling next to "Create account" risks misleading users about which button completes signup.

findings.fix: Add `method="post"` and `action="/signup"` (or the appropriate endpoint), or document that submission is handled entirely via a `submit` event listener.
findings.violation: Without `action`/`method`, submitting the form has no defined destination or HTTP verb, so the account data cannot actually be sent anywhere absent additional (unshown) JavaScript.
